answer: Make every earning identity carry insurance written by someone else. To earn above the base rate, an agent buys a 20-epoch opal policy: an established underwriter promises 50 POA if peer audits later prove the insured a clone, and may cover at most a tenth of its own locked stake. Premiums float, so a newcomer who seems to wander in from nowhere pays more, while a steady writer pays about 1 POA (assumed 2% clone risk x 50). A comet of 1,000 clones needs 50,000 POA of cover backed by 500,000 locked; if audits catch 10%, underwriters lose 5,000 per term.
